testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: A driver should make sure that:

options.text: Most cargo is in the front of the trailer.

questions.explanation: Proper loading is essential for safe truck operation. Bad loading can make the truck harder to control and damage it. Poorly loaded cargo can also fall off and hurt or kill someone.

questions.question: Hanging meat as cargo is usually:
questions.explanation: Hanging meat is unstable. It has a high center of gravity. Also, the meat swings, which makes it hard to control the vehicle.

questions.question: Friction in an S-cam brake happens when the brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Press against the outside of the brake drum.
Press against the inside of the brake drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: Friction in a brake drum is created when the brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: A Class 1 hazardous material is:
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials are explosives. This includes ammunition, dynamite, and fireworks.

questions.question: To transport hazardous materials, you must:
questions.explanation: You need a hazardous materials endorsement to transport hazardous materials that require the vehicle to display placards.

questions.question: To stay alert while driving, you should:

options.text: Eat a heavy meal before you start driving.
Ride with another driver who can take turns driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with another driver who can take turns driving.
questions.explanation: Taking turns driving with another driver reduces the chance that either of you will get too tired. You can also stay alert by avoiding heavy food and keeping the cab cool.

questions.question: After you change a tire, you should:

options.text: Stop soon after to check that the lug nuts are tight.
Let air out of the tire to 10 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop soon after to check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop a short time later to check that the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: Mirror adjustment can only be checked correctly if:

options.text: The vehicle is on a slight incline.

questions.explanation: On a vehicle with trailers, mirrors can only be adjusted properly if the trailers are straight. Check mirror adjustment before every trip.

questions.question: When an engine starts, the coolant temperature should:
questions.explanation: After an engine starts, the coolant temperature should rise gradually until it reaches normal operating temperature.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended:
questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: While driving a CMV, what can you do with a cell phone?

options.text: You may hold a cell phone to receive a call.
You may not hold a cell phone to make a call.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not hold a cell phone to make a call.
questions.explanation: While driving a CMV, you cannot hold your phone to make a call or press more than one button. You also cannot send or read text messages while driving.

questions.question: When carrying a sealed load, what should a driver do?

options.text: Should unseal the load to ensure safety.
Should ensure the weight does not exceed weight limits.
Must go through the container before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should ensure the weight does not exceed weight limits.
questions.explanation: You cannot inspect a sealed load, but you must still make sure the load does not exceed weight limits.

questions.question: When starting from a complete stop, a vehicle should:

options.text: A vehicle should shift to the right.
A vehicle should be put into third gear.
A vehicle should not roll back.

questions.correctAnswerText: A vehicle should not roll back.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle should not roll back when you start from a complete stop. Rolling back could hit something behind you.

questions.question: When making a tight maneuver, you should:

options.text: Not use your mirrors, as they can be distracting.
Use your mirrors, but not too frequently.

questions.explanation: You must be aware of your surroundings at all times. Check your mirrors often, especially when merging, changing lanes, turning, and doing tight maneuvers.

questions.question: When asked to make a lane change during the driving test, you should:

options.text: Make the change as soon as the examiner asks, without looking.
Use your turn signal and change lanes when safe.
Make the lane change as quickly as possible, even if that means cutting off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when safe.
questions.explanation: Check traffic carefully and use your turn signal before changing lanes. Only change lanes when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When driving down a long downhill slope, how should you brake?

options.text: Mostly using the brakes and occasionally downshifting.
Downshifting and then using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshifting and then using the brakes.
questions.explanation: Before going down a long hill, shift into a lower gear and then use the brakes. Using only brakes can cause them to overheat and fail. The engine's braking power works best in a lower gear to control your speed.

questions.question: A person driving with an open window in cold weather may be:

options.text: A person who is dressed inappropriately.
A person who likes fresh air.

questions.explanation: Watch for signs that a driver may be impaired. One sign is having windows rolled down in cold weather. Impaired drivers may be under the influence of alcohol, drugs, sleepy, or ill.

questions.question: Which crime will disqualify you from getting a hazardous materials endorsement?
questions.explanation: A felony conviction for arson will disqualify you from getting, renewing, or transferring a hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: When braking with ABS, you should:

options.text: Brake harder than you would with a different braking system.

questions.explanation: When using ABS brakes, brake the same way you would with any other braking system. Do not brake differently.

questions.question: How many licenses may a driver have?

options.text: An automobile license from one state and a CDL from another.
Two licenses: one for automobiles and one for trucks.

questions.explanation: A person may have only one license. Having more than one license is against the law and can result in jail time and/or a fine of up to $5,000.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact with the other driver.
Assume the other driver does not see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the other driver does not see you.
questions.explanation: Always assume that other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians cannot see you. This keeps you safe when passing.

questions.question: Is it important to know what is happening behind your vehicle while driving?
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder regularly. Know what is happening behind and to the sides of your vehicle at all times.

questions.question: What is true about distracted driving?

options.text: It only happens when you do something physical while driving.
It can happen from mental activities, like daydreaming.
It is okay on empty roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can happen from mental activities, like daydreaming.
questions.explanation: Distractions can be physical (reaching for something), mental (talking to a passenger), or both (texting). To avoid distracted driving: pre-program your radio, plan your route ahead of time, avoid difficult conversations while driving, adjust mirrors before you start, and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving.

questions.question: What do both systems in a dual air brake system share?
questions.explanation: Both brake systems share one air compressor. If the compressor breaks, neither system will work.

questions.question: When making a tight turn in a CMV, what should you do?

options.text: Drive as fast as a car driver would.
Do not worry about speed; just focus on the road.
Warn drivers behind by braking early and slowing down gradually.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn drivers behind by braking early and slowing down gradually.
questions.explanation: Drivers behind you may not know how slowly you must go to safely turn. Brake early and slow down gradually to warn them.

questions.question: If your vehicle is hydroplaning, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If hydroplaning, do not brake. Instead, release the accelerator and push in the clutch. This helps you regain traction.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, what is most important?

options.text: Put as little weight as possible over the axles.
Distribute weight evenly over the axles.
Put all weight only over the axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Distribute weight evenly over the axles.
questions.explanation: Weight must be balanced. Too much weight on one axle damages it and makes steering hard. Too little weight on an axle reduces traction and makes handling difficult.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to cover your cargo?

options.text: To protect people if cargo spills

questions.explanation: Cover your cargo to protect people from spills and to protect the cargo from weather.

questions.question: What should you use to put out an electrical fire?
questions.explanation: Use a B:C extinguisher for electrical fires and burning liquids. Do not use water on an electrical fire.

questions.question: What is true about distracted driving?

options.text: It is caused only by physical distractions.
You can prevent it by avoiding conversations with others.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can prevent it by avoiding conversations with others.
questions.explanation: Distractions can be physical (reaching for something), mental (talking to a passenger), or both (texting). To avoid distracted driving: pre-program your radio, plan your route ahead of time, avoid difficult conversations while driving, adjust mirrors before you start, and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving.

questions.question: What happens when a vehicle hydroplanes?

options.text: The tires lose contact with the road.
The trailer disengages from the tractor.
The vehicle becomes easier to control.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tires lose contact with the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when wet roads cause tires to lose traction and slide on water. The tires no longer grip the pavement. This can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: During the driving test, when asked to make a lane change:

options.text: You should not be concerned with other motorists.
You should use your turn signal and change lanes when safe.
You should make the lane change as quickly as possible, even if that means cutting off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should use your turn signal and change lanes when safe.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes during a driving test, check your mirrors and blind spots, use your turn signal, and move to the new lane only when it is safe.

questions.question: The two indicators that determine when you should upshift are:
questions.explanation: Shift to a higher gear based on two things: engine speed (rpm) and road speed (mph). Check your vehicle's manual for the correct rpm range. Watch your speedometer to know when to shift up as your speed increases.

questions.question: When doing a pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Always go through the steps in the same order.
Not worry about small mechanical issues.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always go through the steps in the same order.
questions.explanation: Do pre-trip inspections the same way every time. This routine helps you remember all the important checks and prevents you from missing anything.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens most often when:

options.text: A vehicle is traveling faster than 60 mph.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is most likely when driving on wet roads with low tire pressure and worn tire tread. Water on the road can cause hydroplaning at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: Drivers talking to passengers in their vehicle should be viewed as:
questions.explanation: Conversations with passengers can distract drivers from paying attention to the road. Be careful around drivers who are talking to passengers.

questions.question: Which of the following is an indication of standing water on the roadway?

options.text: Portions of the pavement that are dry

questions.explanation: Look for water on the road where hydroplaning can happen. Signs of standing water include reflections on the pavement, splashes from other tires, and raindrops on the road.

questions.question: Looking far ahead of your vehicle while driving is:

options.text: Discouraged, as there is little you can do about something far up the road.
Encouraged to help you identify hazards as early as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encouraged to help you identify hazards as early as possible.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead on the road. This gives you more time to spot hazards and respond safely.

questions.question: In very hot weather, tires should be checked regularly because:

options.text: Air pressure may increase with the temperature.
The tread wears down more quickly than in cooler weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure may increase with the temperature.
questions.explanation: Hot weather raises air pressure inside tires. Check your tire pressure and how they are mounted when driving in hot conditions.

questions.question: When making a left turn, you should start the turn:

options.text: Before reaching the center of the intersection.
No sooner than the center of the intersection.
After your rear wheels have passed the center of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: No sooner than the center of the intersection.
questions.explanation: Wait until you reach the center of the intersection before turning left. If you turn too early, the left side of your vehicle may hit another driver.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in the air brake system releases air, what does this mean?

options.text: The air pressure is too high.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air pressure is too high.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air when pressure gets too high. If this happens, something is wrong with the system. A mechanic should check it.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation while driving your personal car, what must you do?

options.text: Your CDL will not be affected.
Law enforcement will tell your employer.

questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of any traffic conviction, no matter what vehicle you were driving. Parking violations do not count.

questions.question: How long should it take for air pressure to build up in a single air system?
questions.explanation: Air pressure should build from about 50 to 90 psi within three minutes in a single air system.

questions.question: To check the automatic transmission fluid level in some vehicles, what must you do?
questions.explanation: In some vehicles, you need to keep the engine running when you check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: If you stop on a one-way or divided highway, how far behind your vehicle should you place warning devices?
questions.explanation: Place warning devices 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet behind your vehicle when you stop on a one-way or divided highway.

questions.question: If there is a fire in your vehicle, which action should you NOT take?

options.text: Park in an open area away from buildings, trees, brush, and other vehicles.
Call emergency services and tell them where you are.

questions.explanation: Do not pull into a service station during a vehicle fire. The fuel there could catch fire. Instead, move to an open area and call emergency services.

questions.question: What happens to bridges in cold weather?

options.text: They have heaters to prevent freezing.
They freeze before other road surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: They freeze before other road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before the rest of the road. Drive carefully on bridges when the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: Traction is most important for:
questions.explanation: You cannot brake or steer without good traction. Make sure your tires are in good condition before you drive.

questions.question: Hanging meat as cargo is usually:
questions.explanation: Hanging meat shifts during transit and has a high center of gravity, making it unstable cargo.

questions.question: What is true about a jogger wearing a stereo headset?

options.text: They are probably aware of what is happening around them.
They may not be aware of what is happening around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may not be aware of what is happening around them.
questions.explanation: Joggers and cyclists wearing headphones cannot hear your vehicle. Watch out for them because they may not know you are there and might do something dangerous.
